q: What changed in CEA CO2 Baseline Database version 22.0?
title: CEA CO2 database version 22.0: what changed
short: Version 22.0, published August 2026, adds FY 2025-26: a weighted average of 0.675 t CO2 per MWh, down from 0.710 for FY 2024-25. It also revises FY 2024-25 using actual captive power data in place of provisional figures, and counts renewable generation in the build and combined margins.
audience: Sustainability teams, auditors and carbon project developers in India who track CEA releases

ul: Data for FY 2025-26, including stations commissioned that year; decommissioned units removed.
FY 2024-25 recalculated with actual captive power data instead of provisional data.
Renewable generation counted in the FY 2025-26 build and combined margins.
Database built to version 7.0 of the CDM Tool to calculate the emission factor for an electricity system.
All in t CO2 per MWh, adjusted for cross-border transfers.

p: Use 0.675 for FY 2025-26 electricity in a location-based footprint. Leave earlier years on the factor for their own year unless CEA revised that year and the change is material to you.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills into dated kWh records per meter and site, so whichever CEA factor and version you apply, each Scope 2 figure traces back to the bill and the factor behind it.
